title.en: Cuba considers $100m US aid offer as energy crisis worsens
title.zh: 古巴考虑美国1亿美元援助提议，能源危机恶化

summary.en: Cuba is considering a $100 million aid offer from the United States as the island nation faces worsening energy shortages. Officials have stated it is unclear whether the assistance would be in cash or in-kind.
summary.zh: 古巴正在考虑美国提供的1亿美元援助，因为该岛国正面临日益恶化的能源短缺。官员表示，目前尚不清楚援助将以现金形式还是实物形式提供。

body.en:
The Cuban government says it is open to reviewing a US offer of $100m (£74m) in aid, hours after rare protests over worsening power cuts erupted on the Communist-run island.

Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez said on Thursday that Cuba was "ready to hear the details of the proposal and how it would be implemented".

The shortages have been exacerbated by a US-imposed blockade of oil which has squeezed the country's supplies of essentials such as diesel and fuel oil.

Hospitals have been unable to function normally, and schools and government offices have been forced to close. Tourism, an economic engine for Cuba, has also been impacted.

Cuba has in the past relied on Venezuela and Mexico to supply oil to its refinery system. However, the two countries have largely cut off supplies since US President Donald Trump threatened tariffs on countries that send fuel to Cuba.

On Wednesday, the US state department said it was renewing an offer to "provide generous assistance to the Cuban people".

Last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said that Havana had rejected a previous US offer of humanitarian aid worth $100m (£74m), a claim Cuba denied.

In its statement, the US state department repeated its offer but made it clear that the aid would have to be distributed "in coordination with the Catholic Church and other reliable independent humanitarian organisations", bypassing the Cuban government.

It added that the decision now rested with the Cuban regime "to accept our offer of assistance or deny critical living-saving aid and ultimately be accountable to the Cuban people for standing in the way of critical assistance".

In his response, Cuban Foreign Minister Rodríguez said it was unclear whether the US aid offer would be in cash or in-kind assistance.

He added that "the Cuban government does not, as a matter of practice, reject foreign aid offered in good faith and with genuine aims of cooperation, whether bilateral or multilateral".

He added that the best way the US could help Cuba would be to "de-escalate energy, economic, commercial, and financial blockade measures, which have intensified as never before in recent months".

Thursday's comments by Rodríguez follow a warning from the country's Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy that Cuba had completely run out of diesel and fuel oil.

In an interview with state-run media, de la O Levy said there were limited amounts of gas available, but that Cuba's energy system was in a "critical" state due to the US-led blockade of oil.

Cubans have been suffering from extensive blackouts, some of them nationwide , for months.

body.zh: 古巴政府表示，愿意审查美国提出的 1 亿美元（7400 万英镑）援助提议，数小时前，古巴因停电恶化而爆发罕见的抗议活动。 外交部长布鲁诺·罗德里格斯周四表示，古巴“准备好听取该提案的细节以及如何实施”。 美国实施的石油封锁挤压了该国柴油和燃料油等必需品的供应，加剧了短缺。 医院无法正常运转，学校和政府办公室被迫关闭。作为古巴经济引擎的旅游业也受到了影响。 古巴过去一直依赖委内瑞拉和墨西哥为其炼油系统供应石油。然而，自从美国总统唐纳德·特朗普威胁对向古巴运送燃料的国家征收关税以来，两国已基本切断供应。 周三，美国国务院表示将重新提出“向古巴人民提供慷慨援助”的提议。 上周，美国国务卿马可·卢比奥表示，哈瓦那拒绝了美国之前提出的价值 1 亿美元（7400 万英镑）的人道主义援助，古巴否认了这一说法。 美国国务院在声明中重申了这一提议，但明确表示援助必须“与天主教会和其他可靠的独立人道主义组织协调”来分发，绕过古巴政府。 它补充说，现在的决定取决于古巴政权“接受我们的援助提议还是拒绝重要的救生援助，并最终对阻碍重要援助的古巴人民负责”。 古巴外交部长罗德里格斯在回应中表示，目前尚不清楚美国提供的援助是现金还是实物援助。 他补充说，“实际上，古巴政府不会拒绝出于真诚和真正的合作目的提供的外国援助，无论是双边还是多边的”。 他补充说，美国帮助古巴的最佳方式是“降低能源、经济、商业和金融封锁措施，这些措施近几个月来前所未有地加强”。 在罗德里格斯周四发表评论之前，该国能源部长文森特·德拉奥·利维警告说，古巴的柴油和燃油已经完全耗尽。 德拉奥利维在接受官方媒体采访时表示，可用天然气数量有限，但由于美国主导的石油封锁，古巴的能源系统处于“危急”状态。 几个月来，古巴人一直遭受大范围停电的困扰，其中一些是全国范围的。 周三，在影响古巴东部大部分地区的最新停电之后，数百人走上哈瓦那街头，用燃烧的垃圾堵塞道路，并高喊......

reflection.en: In times of severe need, gestures of aid can transcend political differences and historical tensions. This offer of assistance, even between nations with complex pasts, reflects a fundamental human impulse to alleviate suffering. It reminds us of the biblical call to show kindness, even to those we might consider adversaries, especially when they are in...
reflection.zh: 在极度匮乏之时，援助的姿态可以超越政治分歧和历史紧张关系。这份援助提议，即使是在有着复杂过往的国家之间，也反映了人类减轻苦难的基本冲动。它提醒我们，圣经呼召我们即使对那些我们可能视为对手的人，也要施以善意，尤其是在他们身处困境时。

verse.textEn: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
verse.textZh: 你的仇敌若饿了，就给他饭吃；若渴了，就给他水喝。

title.en: Streeting resigns as health secretary but stops short of launching leadership bid - UK politics live
title.zh: 安吉拉·雷纳表示，在英国税务海关总署澄清其税务问题后，斯塔默应“反思”是否下台——英国政治直播

summary.en: Angela Rayner, the former deputy prime minister, has been cleared by HMRC regarding her tax affairs. This decision potentially paves the way for her to pursue a leadership bid, and she suggested the current leader should consider stepping aside.
summary.zh: 前副首相安吉拉·雷纳已获英国税务海关总署（HMRC）对其税务事宜的清白。这一裁决可能为她竞选领导人铺平道路，她还建议现任领导人应考虑让位。

body.en: Streeting calls on PM to resign and implies that he would stand as a candidate in a leadership contest Al Carns , the defence minister first elected in 2024, will launch his own leadership bid if a contest starts, Sky News is reporting . Asked about this last night, Carns told Sky: “I’m just a humble junior minister.” Unless Labour understands that insecurity on an emotional level as well as on an economic one, we will continue to lose voters who would naturally align with us. Working-class voters have not simply left Labour. Many feel Labour stopped understanding their lives, and so they looked elsewhere. What is the point of Labour if it does not represent Sheffield, Stoke-on-Trent, Barnsley, Swansea and Aberdeen? What is the point of the Labour party if it cannot replace despair and frustration with hope, stability and purpose? The party was founded to give ordinary working people security, dignity and bargaining power over their lives. Continue reading...

reflection.en: In public life, scrutiny is constant, and allegations can cast long shadows. This story reminds us that while falsehoods may gain temporary traction, truth ultimately has a way of enduring and being revealed. For those in leadership, integrity in all matters, great and small, is a foundation upon which trust is built.
reflection.zh: 在公共生活中，审查无处不在，指控可能投下长长的阴影。这个故事提醒我们，虽然谎言可能暂时得势，但真相最终会显露并持久。对于领导者而言，无论大小事务，正直都是建立信任的基石。

verse.textEn: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
verse.textZh: 口吐真言，永远坚立；舌说谎话，只存片时。

title.en: Ukraine hit by second day of large-scale Russian missile and drone strikes
title.zh: 乌克兰连续第二天遭受俄罗斯大规模导弹和无人机袭击

summary.en: Russian forces launched a second consecutive day of extensive missile and drone strikes across Ukraine, with Kyiv experiencing severe attacks. The widespread nature of these assaults has led to warnings that Moscow aims to overwhelm Ukrainian air defense systems, resulting in casualties.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯军队连续第二天对乌克兰发动大规模导弹和无人机袭击，基辅首当其冲，遭受了猛烈攻击。这些广泛的袭击引发了警告，称莫斯科正试图压垮乌克兰的防空系统，并已造成人员伤亡。

body.en: Widespread nature of attacks prompts warnings that Moscow is trying to overwhelm air defence systems Russian missiles and drones are pounding Ukraine for a second day, as almost continuous heavy attacks hit the country, with Kyiv bearing the brunt of an assault that has killed at least eight people, including a 13-year-old, and injured 44 in the capital. The overnight attacks followed heavy daylight raids with missiles and drones across the country on Wednesday, one of the longest single attacks of the war. Continue reading...
body.zh: 袭击的广泛性促使人们发出警告称，莫斯科正试图压倒防空系统。俄罗斯导弹和无人机连续第二天袭击乌克兰，该国几乎连续遭受猛烈袭击，基辅首当其冲，袭击造成至少 8 人死亡，其中包括一名 13 岁儿童，首都 44 人受伤。周三，在白天用导弹和无人机在全国范围内进行大规模袭击之后，发生了夜间袭击，这是战争中持续时间最长的单次袭击之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As Ukraine endures a second day of relentless missile and drone attacks, the scale of suffering can feel overwhelming. Yet, even in the midst of sustained devastation, the biblical promise reminds us that 雅伟's steadfast love never ceases, and His mercies are new every morning. This truth offers a quiet strength, affirming that even when darkness persists, a...
reflection.zh: 乌克兰连续第二天遭受无情导弹和无人机袭击，苦难的规模令人感到难以承受。然而，即使在持续的破坏中，圣经的应许提醒我们，雅伟的慈爱永不止息，祂的怜悯每天早晨都是新的。这个真理提供了一种安静的力量，肯定了即使黑暗持续存在，每天仍有新的恩典来面对。

verse.textEn: Because of Yahweh's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.
verse.textZh: 我们不至消灭，是出于雅伟诸般的慈爱；是因他的怜悯不至断绝。每早晨这都是新的。

title.en: Trump China visit live: ‘US and China should be partners, not rivals’, Xi says after earlier warning on Taiwan
title.zh: 特朗普访华直播：据官方媒体报道，习近平警告称，若台湾问题处理不当，中美可能“陷入冲突”

reflection.en: In a world fraught with geopolitical tensions, leaders bear a heavy responsibility to pursue peace. The warning of potential conflict underscores the constant need for diligent diplomacy and a commitment to de-escalation. Romans 12:18 reminds us that, as far as it depends on us, we are called to live at peace with everyone, a principle that extends to...
reflection.zh: 在一个充满地缘政治紧张的世界里，领导人肩负着追求和平的重任。潜在冲突的警告凸显了持续勤勉外交和致力于缓和局势的必要性。罗马书12:18提醒我们，若是可能，总要尽力与众人和睦，这一原则也适用于国际关系。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Nigel Farage bought £1.4m property in cash shortly after receiving £5m gift
title.zh: 奈杰尔·法拉奇在收到500万英镑赠予后不久，以现金购买了140万英镑的房产

summary.en: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage is facing a parliamentary investigation after reports revealed he bought a £1.4 million property in cash shortly after receiving a £5 million personal gift from a crypto billionaire.
summary.zh: 英国改革党领袖奈杰尔·法拉奇正面临议会调查，此前有报道称，他在收到一位加密货币亿万富翁500万英镑的个人赠予后不久，便以现金购买了一处价值140万英镑的房产。

The revelation came as the Reform UK leader appeared to change his line on the reason for the £5m gift, saying in an interview on Thursday that it was a “reward” for campaigning for Brexit for 27 years. Continue reading...

reflection.en: News of a political leader receiving a substantial gift and making a large cash purchase raises questions about financial transparency and the influence of wealth. The Bible reminds us that the love of money can be a root of many evils, prompting us to consider the ethical implications when significant sums change hands, especially in public life. This...
reflection.zh: 一位政治领袖收到巨额赠予并进行大笔现金购买的消息，引发了人们对财务透明度和财富影响力的疑问。圣经提醒我们，贪财是万恶之根，这促使我们思考当大笔资金易手时，尤其是在公共生活中，其所带来的道德影响。这种情况强调了领导层持续需要保持诚信和问责制。

verse.textEn: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
verse.textZh: 贪财是万恶之根。

title.en: For anxious Taiwan, Trump’s silence after Xi talks is best possible outcome
title.zh: 对于焦虑的台湾来说，特朗普在习特会后的沉默是最好的结果

summary.en: Taiwan expressed relief after a summit between the Chinese and US presidents, as initial fears that the US might withdraw its longstanding support for the island receded. Observers had previously described Taiwan as an anxious bystander ahead of the talks.
summary.zh: 在中美两国总统峰会后，台湾松了一口气，此前对美国可能放弃长期支持的担忧有所缓解。观察人士曾将台湾描述为峰会前焦虑的旁观者。

body.en: Island breathes sigh of relief as fears recede that US could jettison longstanding support Trump China visit live – latest updates Before this week’s summit between the Chinese and US presidents, Taiwan had been cast as the anxious bystander. Observers suggested that Taipei feared the unpredictable and transactional Donald Trump might overturn Washington’s longstanding support for the island democracy , which Beijing claims as a breakaway province, during Thursday and Friday’s talks. Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着人们对美国可能放弃长期支持特朗普访华的担忧消退，台湾松了一口气——最新动态在本周的中美两国元首峰会之前，台湾一直被视为焦虑的旁观者。观察人士表示，台北担心不可预测且交易性强的唐纳德·特朗普可能会在周四和周五的会谈中推翻华盛顿对台湾民主制度的长期支持，北京称台湾是一个分离的省份。继续阅读...

reflection.en: For those caught in geopolitical uncertainties, moments of relief can feel like a dawn after a long night of worry. This story reflects how a vulnerable island nation experienced a temporary reprieve from its anxieties. In life's unpredictable seasons, we often find that weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes with the morning.
reflection.zh: 对于那些身处地缘政治不确定性中的人们来说，解脱的时刻就像漫长忧虑之夜后的黎明。这个故事反映了一个脆弱的岛屿国家如何从焦虑中获得暂时的喘息。在生命不可预测的季节里，我们常会发现，虽然哭泣可能持续一夜，但喜乐却随着清晨而来。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: UK: Health Secretary Wes Streeting resigns, likely in bid to topple PM Keir Starmer
title.zh: 英国：卫生大臣韦斯·斯特里廷辞职，可能是为了推翻首相凯尔·斯塔默

summary.en: Two Labour Party politicians have positioned themselves to challenge Prime Minister Keir Starmer for the leadership. Health Secretary Wes Streeting resigned, and Angela Rayner said her tax affairs were back in order.

body.zh: 两名工党政客已准备好挑战总理基尔·斯塔默（Keir Starmer）的领导权。卫生部长韦斯·斯特里廷辞职，安吉拉·雷纳表示她的税务事务已恢复正常。 英国工党的两位重量级人物周四试图挑战首相基尔·斯塔默，尽管他们都没有宣布直接挑战，而是似乎鼓励这位四面楚歌的党魁自愿让路。 卫生部长韦斯·斯特里廷采取了最直接的行动，成为斯塔默内阁中第一位辞职的高级成员，以抗议工党上周在地方和地区选举中惨败。 但前党副主席安吉拉·雷纳也向媒体发出黎明警报，称促使她辞职的税务丑闻现已解决，这被解读为间接的意向声明。 斯塔默周一的好斗演讲和周二紧张的内阁会议都未能平息选举失败后的局势。就在两年前，斯塔默和工党赢得了绝大多数席位，承诺结束十多年来保守党领导的、以频繁更换总理为特征的混乱局面。 斯特里廷在网上发表了一封冗长的辞职信，但没有进一步发表评论。他首先回顾了他在担任该职位期间所取得的成功。 “这些都是我继续留任的充分理由，”斯特里廷写道，“但正如你从本周早些时候我们的谈话中了解到的那样，在对你的领导力失去信心后，我得出的结论是，这样做是不光彩和没有原则的。” 斯特里廷称上周的选举结果“无论是在失败的规模还是失败的后果方面都是前所未有的”。 他说：“在我们国家的历史上，这是第一次，民族主义者掌控了英国的每一个角落，其中包括以奈杰尔·法拉奇和改革英国为代表的危险的英国民族主义。” 这指的是工党在边境以北输给苏格兰民族党、在威尔士大本营中输给民族主义者格莱德·西姆鲁以及在英国各地（尤其是英格兰）奈杰尔·法拉奇的右翼民粹主义者。 斯特里廷现年 43 岁，具有伦敦工人阶级背景，2015 年成为议员。他表示，斯塔默有很多地方让他钦佩，但他在信中也列出了一系列失败和缺点。 与此同时，前工党副党魁安吉拉·雷纳(Angela Rayner)的团队于当地时间周四早上6点整动员起来，让英国媒体知道，国家税务机关现在认为导致她去年辞职的财产税丑闻已经得到解决。 她接受了采访...

summary.en: President Trump was welcomed by President Xi Jinping in Beijing for what will be a whirlwind tour.

body.en:
Donald Trump and Xi Jinping have been holding talks in the Chinese capital, Beijing, with a raft of meetings and events taking place on Thursday and Friday.

The US leader was greeted with a gun salute, cheering children and a tour of the stunning 15th Century Temple of Heaven.

Trump is also joined in Beijing by tech bosses, including Tesla's Elon Musk and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and Trump's son Eric.

On Thursday evening, a lavish banuquet at the Great Hall of the People was held in honour of the occasion.

BBC reporters were able to see the banquet menu, with the main course including lobster in tomato soup, Beijing roast duck and pan-fried pork bun.

In a banquet speech, President Xi called it a "historic visit", adding "the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation" and "Make America great again" can go hand in hand.

China-US relations are the most important bilateral relations in the world, Xi says.

Their relations concern the well-being of the two countries of 1.7 billion population, and the interests of over 8 billion people in the world, he added.

He then invited Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to visit the White House on 24 September.

Among those spotted at Thurday's banquet were Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Apple CEO Tim Cook, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Eric and Lara Trump.

Trump landed in Beijing on Wednesday evening, where he was greeted by youths waving American and Chinese flags as he walked the red carpet with Vice President of China Han Zheng.

On Thursday, Trump was welcomed at an arrival ceremony with Xi at China's Great Hall of the People.

After shaking hands, Trump and Xi walked the red carpet and inspected Chinese troops who lined up in impeccably neat rows.

Dozens of children also lined up along the red carpet and waved mini flags and bouquets.

Joining Trump on his trip to China are some of the US's top business leaders, including Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, and Larry Fink of BlackRock.

Jensen Huang, the boss of Nvidia, a company which has been central to the US-China technology rivalry, was reportedly a last-minute addition.

The leaders then held highly anticipated bilateral talks in the Great Hall of the People.

"Currently transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe and the international situation is fluid and turbulent".

"We've gotten along, when there were difficulties we worked it out. I would call you and you would call me," Trump said.

After two hours of talks, the leaders then visited the Temple of Heaven, an ancient complex of temples in Beijing and a major tourist attraction.

The historic site is where emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties would offer sacrifices and pray for bountiful harvests.

title.en: Who is Mario Draghi, this year's Charlemagne Prize winner?
title.zh: 今年的查理曼奖获得者马里奥·德拉吉是谁？

summary.en: The Charlemagne Prize honors those who advance European unity. This year's winner is Italy's Mario Draghi, a former European Central Bank chief and a key architect of European stability during a time of economic crisis.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Charlemagne Prize honors those who advance European unity. This year's winner is Italy's Mario Draghi, a former European Central Bank chief and a key architect of European stability during a time of economic crisis.

The former head of the European Central Bank Mario Draghi was presented with the prestigious Charlemagne Prize at a ceremony in Aachen, western Germany, on May 14.

"You took charge of the euro during a time of crisis, and you stabilized the euro and the eurozone," Chancellor Friedrich Merz said during his speech honoring Draghi. 

With his 2024 report on the future of European competitiveness, dubbed the Draghi Report , Merz said Draghi had "pointed the way toward reform with his unsparing analysis."

"I think you'll understand why his friends call him Super Mario," the German chancellor joked.

Draghi is likely mostly remembered as the head of the Frankfurt-based European Central Bank (ECB), who worked to stabilize the eurozone during turbulent times. But he had many other career stops along the way.

Draghi started out as a professor of economics in Italy. Later he worked at the World Bank  and Goldman Sachs. Over the years, he served on the board of several Italian banks and companies.

From 2006 until 2011 he was the governor of the Bank of Italy, the country's central bank. It was during his time there that problems started to surface in the US subprime mortgage market. By 2008, the situation turned into a global crisis, especially following the collapse of the investment bank Lehman Brothers, that wreaked havoc on economies around the world.

Draghi was selected to run the ECB in 2011, in the middle of this turmoil. By this time, the global financial crisis had triggered a Europen debt crisis. This led to austerity measures and bailouts in some eurozone countries, most notably Greece .

Draghi tirelessly defended the single currency and became known for saying the ECB would do "whatever it takes" to stop the euro from failing. This was seen as a turning point in the eurozone crisis.

In 2015, the bank started to buy large amounts of bonds to inject money into the economy. Called "quantitative easing" the program was meant to combat low inflation and weak economic growth.

Critics argue that these policies kept interest rates too low for too long. The bank's quantitative easing program expanded its mandate and meant some governments had less incentive to work on structural reforms.   

"While not every single decision by Draghi can be seen, in hindsight, as successful, the overall balance is strongly positive," said Francesco Papadia, a senior fellow at the Brussels-based think tank Bruegel.

body.zh: 查理曼奖旨在表彰那些促进欧洲团结的人。今年的获奖者是意大利前欧洲央行行长马里奥·德拉吉(Mario Draghi)，他是经济危机时期欧洲稳定的关键设计师。 5 月 14 日，欧洲央行前行长马里奥·德拉吉 (Mario Draghi) 在德国西部亚琛举行的颁奖典礼上荣获著名的查理曼奖。 德国总理弗里德里希·默茨在向德拉吉致敬的讲话中表示：“您在危机时期掌控了欧元，稳定了欧元和欧元区。” 默茨在其关于欧洲竞争力未来的 2024 年报告（被称为“德拉吉报告”）中表示，德拉吉“用他毫不留情的分析为改革指明了道路”。 “我想你会明白为什么他的朋友称他为超级马里奥，”德国总理开玩笑说。 德拉吉最被人铭记的身份可能是总部位于法兰克福的欧洲央行（ECB）行长，他在动荡时期致力于稳定欧元区。但在此过程中，他的职业生涯还经历了许多其他的停留。 德拉吉最初是意大利的一名经济学教授。后来他在世界银行和高盛工作。多年来，他曾在多家意大利银行和公司的董事会任职。 2006年至2011年，他担任该国中央银行意大利央行行长。正是在他任职期间，美国次级抵押贷款市场的问题开始浮出水面。到了 2008 年，情况演变成了一场全球危机，特别是雷曼兄弟投资银行倒闭后，给世界各地的经济造成了严重破坏。 2011 年，德拉吉在这场动荡期间被选为欧洲央行行长。此时，全球金融危机已引发欧债危机。这导致一些欧元区国家（尤其是希腊）采取紧缩措施和救助。 德拉吉孜孜不倦地捍卫单一货币，并因表示欧洲央行将“不惜一切代价”阻止欧元崩溃而闻名。这被视为欧元区危机的转折点。 2015年，该银行开始购买大量债券，向经济注入资金。该计划被称为“量化宽松”，旨在应对低通胀和疲软的经济增长。 批评者认为，这些政策使利率维持在过低水平的时间过长。央行的量化宽松计划扩大了其职责范围，意味着一些政府进行结构性改革的动力减弱。 布鲁塞尔智库布鲁盖尔高级研究员弗朗西斯科·帕帕迪亚表示：“虽然事后看来，德拉吉的每一个决定都不是成功的，但总体平衡是非常积极的。” 欧洲“在……期间由他执掌欧洲央行，受益匪浅”

title.en: Warning of record global temperatures as chance of very strong El Niño grows
title.zh: 强烈厄尔尼诺现象的可能性增加，全球气温将创历史新高

summary.en: As El Niño develops this year, scientists are increasingly confident it could be one of the strongest on record with global consequences, as Simon King explains.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
New forecasts show increasing confidence that the developing El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean could be one of the strongest on record with warnings of record global temperatures and huge humanitarian impacts.

Parts of the Pacific have been warming rapidly with data this week showing sea surface temperatures around 0.5C above normal - one threshold used to suggest the onset of El Niño, a natural warming of the Pacific.

It is expected to strengthen over the next few months, peaking potentially as a very strong - or so-called super El Niño - in the autumn.

Scientists are concerned about the consequences it could have on global weather patterns, including the likelihood of 2027 being the warmest year on record.

In their latest outlook, the National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) suggest El Niño will begin within the month.

They have increased the confidence to a two-in-three chance that it will be strong or even very strong by this winter.

The rate of warming seen in the tropical Pacific over the last few weeks has been rapid.

Nathanial Johnson, a meteorologist at NOAA described it as a "rare occurrence" should it continue at the current pace - going from the La Niña (a similar cooling pattern) we saw in winter to a potentially strong El Niño, within a year.

The Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) in Australia also forecasts El Niño using a slightly stricter criterion where sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific must exceed 0.8C above average.

They also look for indications that the trade winds in the western Pacific have reversed; signalling that the warming ocean is beginning to influence the atmosphere.

Spring forecasts of El Niño have historically been quite poor, but forecasters have been much more confident than normal this year.

While El Niño forms across the tropical Pacific, forecasters look at one region in particular called the Niño3.4, monitoring a three-monthly average of the sea surface temperature compared to the long-term average.

Forecasts from the European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), NOAA and BoM are all pretty much aligned in their outcomes.

In the latest prediction from the ECMWF, more than half of their forecast models suggest a temperature of over 2.5C by the autumn.

BoM forecasts are also confidently showing the possibility of a very strong El Niño to develop later this year.

Some forecast data is even suggesting the temperature could exceed 3C, surpassing the current known peak of 2.7C recorded in 1877.

It should be noted this was a very different era with limited observations and so there remains a lot of uncertainty in the reported temperature.

title.en: 'Floating armoury' ship reportedly seized by Iran
title.zh: 据报道伊朗扣押了“浮动军械库”船

summary.en: A vessel said to be a “floating armoury” in the Gulf of Oman has been seized by Iranian military personnel, according to reports.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A vessel reportedly operating as a "floating armoury" in the Gulf of Oman has been seized by Iranian military personnel, according to the maritime risk management company Vanguard.

The ship is now "bound for Iranian territorial waters", the UK's Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) organisation said.

BBC Verify has checked ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic which shows the vessel - identified by Vanguard as the Honduras-flagged Hui Chuan - last broadcast its location 70km (40 miles) north-east of Fujairah in the UAE on Wednesday.

Hui Chuan's operators told Vanguard it was operating as a floating armoury which stores weapons for security firms who protect ships at sea from attack by pirates.

The BBC has previously reported how these vessels are based in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Gulf of Oman so security guards can easily collect and drop off weapons and ammunition.

Location data shows the ship has spent the last month off the north-east coasts of Oman and the UAE.

The apparent seizure of Hui Chuan comes after an Indian-flagged vessel was attacked off the coast of Oman on Wednesday, according to Indian officials.

The Haji Ali "reportedly sank" off the coast of Oman, following a suspected explosion believed to have been caused by a "drone or missile", according to Vanguard.

"All Indian crew on board are safe and we thank the Omani authorities for rescuing them," Indian authorities said on Thursday.

Ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic shows the 57m (187ft) vessel left Berbera Port in Somalia on 6 May. Its intended destination was Sharjah in the UAE, the Indian shipping ministry said.

The ship was carrying livestock "when a fire reportedly broke out onboard, forcing the crew to abandon ship before the vessel sank," Vanguard said.

Fourteen crew members were transferred by Oman Coast Guard units to the country's Diba Port, according to Indian officials.

The situation in the Strait of Hormuz was discussed during talks on Thursday between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart President Xi Jinping in Beijing.

The White House said Xi had "made clear China's opposition to the militarization of the Strait".

"The two sides agreed that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open to support the free flow of energy," according to a readout issued by the US after the meeting.
body.zh: 据海事风险管理公司先锋集团称，一艘据报道在阿曼湾充当“浮动军械库”的船只已被伊朗军事人员扣押。 英国海事贸易运营组织（UKMTO）表示，这艘船现在“驶往伊朗领海”。 BBC verify 检查了 MarineTraffic 的船舶跟踪数据，该数据显示这艘船（被 Vanguard 确认为悬挂洪都拉斯国旗的 Hui Chuan 号）最后一次广播其位置于周三，位于阿联酋富查伊拉东北 70 公里（40 英里）处。 汇川的经营者告诉先锋集团，它是一个浮动军械库，为保护海上船只免受海盗袭击的安全公司储存武器。 英国广播公司此前曾报道过这些船只如何驻扎在红海、亚丁湾和阿曼湾，以便保安人员可以轻松收集和投放武器和弹药。 位置数据显示，这艘船上个月一直在阿曼和阿联酋东北海岸附近航行。 据印度官员称，周三，一艘悬挂印度国旗的船只在阿曼海岸附近遭到袭击，汇川号被明显扣押。 据先锋集团称，哈吉·阿里号据报道在阿曼海岸附近“沉没”，原因是疑似由“无人机或导弹”引起的爆炸。 印度当局周四表示：“船上所有印度船员都很安全，我们感谢阿曼当局营救他们。” MarineTraffic 的船舶跟踪数据显示，这艘 57m（187 英尺）长的船只于 5 月 6 日离开索马里伯贝拉港。印度航运部表示，其预定目的地是阿联酋的沙迦。 先锋集团表示，这艘船当时正在载运牲畜，“据报道船上发生火灾，迫使船员在船沉没前弃船”。 据印度官员称，阿曼海岸警卫队将 14 名船员转移到该国的迪巴港。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平周四在北京举行会谈，讨论了霍尔木兹海峡的局势。 白宫表示，习近平已“明确表明中国反对海峡军事化”。 根据美国在会后发布的一份声明，“双方同意霍尔木兹海峡必须保持开放，以支持能源自由流动”。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to truth, discernment, and honest speech. Philippians 4:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with discernment and truthful speech, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到真理、分辨与诚实。Philippians 4:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以分辨与诚实表达来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — think about such things.
verse.textZh: 凡是真实的、可敬的、公义的、清洁的、可爱的、有美名的，这些事你们都要思念。

title.en: Iran war tests India's multi-alignment diplomacy
title.zh: 伊朗战争考验印度多边外交

summary.en: New Delhi is proud of its carefully balanced ties with rival nations in the Middle East. But this diplomatic strategy might be reaching its breaking point.
summary.zh: 新德里对其在中东地区与竞争对手国家之间精心平衡的关系感到自豪。然而，这种外交策略可能正达到其崩溃点。

body.en:
New Delhi is proud of its carefully balanced ties with rival nations in the Middle East. But this diplomatic strategy might be reaching its breaking point.

India has long taken pride in doing what few major powers could manage. It bought oil from Iran , built defense ties with Israel , strengthened relations with the US and expanded economic links with the Gulf monarchies, while insisting it would not be drawn into regional camps or formal alliances .

The Iran war , however, is pushing that formula to its limits. India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi seems to be feeling the pressure — he is set to embark on a diplomatic tour on Friday that will see him visit the United Arab Emirates and four European countries in seven days.

For New Delhi, the Iran conflict is more than an energy crisis unfolding in a distant region . It is a direct challenge to the core assumption behind India's foreign policy in the Middle East, namely that it can maintain its own strategic autonomy while cultivating ties with every major power in the region, irrespective of their rivalries.

Amitabh Mattoo, dean of the School of International Studies at Delhi's Jawaharlal Nehru University, says India spent decades perfecting a balancing act that was rooted in "hard-headed realism."

"But the Iran conflict has made the geometry far more unforgiving. Strategic autonomy works best in a fluid multipolar order," Mattoo told DW.

"It becomes harder when rival camps demand political loyalty, sanctions compliance, and security alignment all at once," he added.

"If push comes to shove, India's first instinct will always be to protect economic stability and energy security. No government in New Delhi can afford prolonged oil shocks, shipping disruptions in Hormuz , or domestic inflation spirals," he said.

But he stops short of labeling such moves as a rupture with Washington or Tel Aviv.

"The US is indispensable for India's larger strategic future: technology, defense, Indo-Pacific balancing, and access to global capital. Israel remains a critical defense and intelligence partner. The Gulf is central to energy, remittances, and diaspora stability. Iran matters for geography and continental access," Mattoo said.

What the crisis has exposed, in his assessment, is something larger than a policy dilemma.

"India is no longer a bystander in West Asia. Its dependence on the region means every escalation there now directly tests India's great-power ambitions. Strategic autonomy is no longer a slogan. It is a stress test," he said.

"New Delhi wants strategic autonomy, but the deeper its global integration becomes, the harder it is to remain geopolitically non-aligned in moments of major conflict. Neutrality in a polarized West Asia is becoming less a position and more a luxury,"...
body.zh: 新德里对其与中东敌对国家精心平衡的关系感到自豪。但这一外交策略可能已达到极限。 长期以来，印度一直为自己所做的事情而感到自豪，而很少有大国能够做到这一点。它从伊朗购买石油，与以色列建立防务关系，加强与美国的关系，扩大与海湾君主国的经济联系，同时坚称不会加入地区阵营或正式联盟。 然而，伊朗战争正在将这一公式推向极限。印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪似乎感受到了压力——他定于周五开始外交之旅，在 7 天内访问阿拉伯联合酋长国和四个欧洲国家。 对于新德里来说，伊朗冲突不仅仅是遥远地区正在发生的能源危机。这是对印度中东外交政策背后核心假设的直接挑战，即印度可以保持自己的战略自主权，同时与该地区每个主要大国培养关系，无论它们之间存在怎样的竞争。 德里贾瓦哈拉尔尼赫鲁大学国际研究学院院长阿米塔布·马图表示，印度花了几十年的时间完善植根于“头脑冷静的现实主义”的平衡行为。 马图告诉德国之声：“但伊朗冲突让局势变得更加无情。战略自主权在流动的多极秩序中效果最佳。” 他补充说：“当敌对阵营同时要求政治忠诚、制裁合规和安全协调时，事情就会变得更加困难。” “如果事情到了紧要关头，印度的第一反应永远是保护经济稳定和能源安全。新德里的任何政府都无法承受长期的石油危机、霍尔木兹海峡的航运中断或国内通货膨胀的螺旋式上升，”他说。 但他没有将此类举动视为与华盛顿或特拉维夫的决裂。 马图说：“美国对于印度更大的战略未来是不可或缺的：技术、国防、印太平衡以及获得全球资本的机会。以色列仍然是重要的国防和情报伙伴。海湾地区对于能源、汇款和侨民稳定至关重要。伊朗对于地理位置和大陆准入至关重要。” 在他看来，这场危机暴露出的不仅仅是政策困境。 “印度不再是西亚的旁观者。它对该地区的依赖意味着现在该地区的每一次升级都直接考验印度的大国野心。战略自主不再是一个口号。这是一次压力测试，”他说。 “新德里想要战略自主权，但其全球一体化越深入，在重大冲突时刻保持地缘政治不结盟就越困难。在两极分化的西亚，中立正变得不再是一种立场，而是一种奢侈，”……

reflection.en: India's multi-alignment diplomacy seeks to navigate complex international rivalries by maintaining balanced ties, a strategy that requires careful guidance. When global tensions escalate, even the most meticulously planned approaches can face a breaking point, highlighting the constant need for wise counsel in leadership. reflection.zh: 印度奉行的多边外交旨在通过维持与竞争对手的平衡关系来驾驭复杂的国际对抗，这是一种需要审慎指导的策略。当全球紧张局势升级时，即使是最周密的计划也可能面临崩溃点，这突显了领导层持续需要明智的忠告。这提醒我们，国家和个人一样，从寻求和听取健全的建议中受益，以避免陷入混乱。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Ukraine rescuers pull dead from rubble of Kyiv flats after massive Russian strikes
title.zh: 俄罗斯大规模袭击造成两人死亡后，救援人员搜寻基辅公寓废墟

summary.en: Officials report that two people were killed and children were among the injured after Russia launched drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, hitting flats in Kyiv.
summary.zh: 官员称，俄罗斯对乌克兰发动无人机和导弹袭击，击中基辅公寓，造成两人死亡，其中包括儿童在内的多人受伤。

body.en:
At least eight people have been killed, including a 12-year-old girl, in Kyiv after Russia launched a massive overnight drone and missile strikes on the Ukrainian capital and other regions, officials have said.

The victims' bodies were pulled from the rubble of a partially destroyed apartment building in Kyiv, where rescuers are still searching for at least 20 people feared missing, Ukraine's emergencies service DSNS said.

It said 45 people, including two children, were injured. Friday has been declared a day of mourning in the city.

It is the third day in a row Ukraine has reported deaths, as Moscow ramps up its assault after a three-day ceasefire expired on Monday.

The overnight barrage saw more than 670 drones and 56 missiles targeting the country, President Volodomyr Zelensky said. This is among the largest attacks Russia has mounted since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The strikes hit more than 180 sites across Ukraine, including more than 50 residential buildings, Zelensky added.

He said a total of more than 1,560 Russian drones had targeted Ukrainian cities since Tuesday night, describing Moscow's assault as "definitely not the actions of those who believe the war is coming to an end" and urging allies to hold Moscow accountable.

After an urgent meeting with Ukraine's top military and security officials, Zelensky said a "significant number" of drones were shot down, with an "overall interception rate" of 93%.

But the same figures for missiles stood at 73%, the Ukrainian leader said, admitting that the "key challenge" remained in how to defend against Russian ballistic missiles.

He said the "priority number one" was to secure more deliveries of "anti-ballistic systems and missiles for them".

Ukraine has repeatedly said it has a massive shortage of US-made Patriot missile systems which can effectively intercept Russian ballistics.

Reacting to the latest Russian attacks, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen accused Moscow of indiscriminately targeting civilians.

"Another night of death and destruction," she wrote in a post on X. "While Russia openly mocks diplomatic efforts, we continue to strengthen Ukraine.

"We are finalising a €6 billion ($7bn; £5bn) drone support package. And we keep the pressure on Russia's war economy with ever tougher sanctions," von der Leyen added.

In Kyiv, a search and rescue operation began early Thursday to look for people under the rubble of a nine-storey apartment block in the south-western Darnytskyi district.

Police said two men, aged 21 and 30, and a woman, who has not yet been identified, were found dead in the rubble of the building's destroyed entrance.

body.zh: 官员称，俄罗斯连夜对乌克兰发动大规模袭击，造成两人死亡，数十人受伤。 乌克兰总理尤利娅·斯维里登科表示，这“对基辅来说是一个特别困难的夜晚”，在首都遭受导弹和无人机联合袭击后，救援人员正在一栋住宅楼的废墟中进行搜索。 该市市长表示，至少 40 人受伤，其中包括两名儿童。其中约31人正在医院接受治疗。 这是乌克兰连续第三天报告死亡事件，为期三天的停火周一到期后，莫斯科加大了攻击力度。 总统弗洛多米尔·泽连斯基表示，在夜间的密集攻击中，全国发射了 670 多架无人机和 56 枚导弹。这是俄罗斯自 2022 年开始全面入侵以来发动的最大规模袭击之一。 在首都，搜救行动周四早些时候开始，在一座夜间遭到袭击的九层公寓楼废墟下寻找人员。 基辅市长维塔利·克利奇科(Vitaliy Klychko)参观了这座大楼，他说有18套公寓被毁。他还表示，袭击扰乱了该市的供水。 泽伦斯基表示，到目前为止，已有数十人从该建筑中获救，其他住宅楼、一所学校、一家兽医诊所和其他基础设施也遭到破坏。 乌克兰总理斯维里登科表示，在这次大规模袭击中，俄罗斯无人机飞越了乌克兰大部分地区，克列缅丘克、白采尔科维、哈尔科夫、苏梅和敖德萨等地区也受到攻击。 “乌克兰需要帮助加强其防空能力，”她在社交媒体上写道。 “这是拯救我们的人民和城市的唯一途径。” 乌克兰外交部长安德烈·西比哈谴责俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的“野蛮袭击”，他说这表明莫斯科正在追求“侵略和恐怖”而不是和平。 他指出，袭击发生在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平举行重要峰会期间，并敦促两位领导人向俄罗斯施加压力。 “我确信美国和中国领导人对莫斯科有足够的影响力来告诉普京最终结束战争，”他说。 最近的袭击发生在美国斡旋的为期三天的停火协议于周一晚些时候到期后不久。 俄罗斯和乌克兰都报告称，停战期间发生了多次违规行为——主要是在广阔的前线——但没有发生大规模空袭。 周三，乌克兰又从俄罗斯发射了 892 架无人机，造成另一场重大袭击，造成 6 人死亡。 周四上午，泽连斯基表示，自周二晚上以来，共有超过 1,560 架俄罗斯无人机瞄准了乌克兰城市。 他将俄罗斯的大规模袭击描述为“绝对不是......

reflection.en: The news of lives lost and children injured in these attacks brings profound sorrow. In moments of such senseless violence and suffering, we remember that even Jesus, faced with human grief, wept. His tears remind us that it is right to mourn with those who mourn, and that empathy is a sacred response to the pain of the world.
reflection.zh: 这些袭击造成生命逝去、儿童受伤的消息，带来了深切的悲痛。在面对这种毫无意义的暴力和苦难时，我们记得即使是耶稣，在面对人类的悲伤时，也曾哭泣。祂的眼泪提醒我们，与哀哭的人同哭是正确的，而同情心是对世界痛苦的神圣回应。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Tunisia sliding into authoritarianism, experts say
title.zh: 专家称突尼斯正滑向威权主义

summary.en: Experts warn that Tunisia is moving towards authoritarianism as the government increases pressure on opposition figures, journalists, and civil society, raising concerns about deepening repression and the erosion of democracy.
summary.zh: 专家警告称，突尼斯正滑向威权主义，政府加大对反对派人士、记者和公民社会的施压，引发了对镇压加剧和民主稳步瓦解的担忧。

body.en:
The Tunisian government is ramping up pressure on opposition figures, journalists and civil society — raising fresh fears of deepening repression and the steady dismantling of democracy.

Human rights in Tunisia are a growing case for concern. On Tuesday, courts upheld the sentencing of two prominent Tunisian journalists accused of financial crimes. But media rights group say the ruling was a case of "judicial harassment," and argued that the charges leveled lacked evidence.

Prior to the hearing, Amnesty International sounded the alarm, accusing Tunisian authorities of intensifying their pressure on non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and using legal means to disband such groups. NGO that advocate for human rights, migrant protection , election monitoring and against corruption are most affected .

"Dozens of NGOs run the risk of being dissolved, while others are being prosecuted," Safia Rayan of Amnesty International told DW. "The crackdown on civil society and independent media outlets is intensifying and threatening their existence."

Last week, the UN ' s High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, called on Tunisia to end its repression of opposition members and civil society groups. Speaking in Geneva, Türk said human rights activists were being criminalized.

The fate of 84-year-old Rached Ghannouchi , the chairman of the moderate Islamic Ennahda party, has also sparked concern. He ranks among the country ' s most prominent prisoners, and has been handed jail sentences now adding up to around 50 years behind bars according to Reuters news agency.

Tunisian President Kais Saied, elected to office in 2019, has been consolidating power since 2021. He's sidelined the Tunisia's parliament, weakened its judiciary and has action against opposition members and critics .

The Democratic Erosion Consortium, a US organization specialized in examining democratic structures, describes Saied's style of government as "stealth authoritarianism," whereby democratic institutions are undermined gradually. All that remains, according to the group, is a "facade of a democracy."

Tunisian authorities have been cracking down on dissidents for some time now. In April 2025, a Tunis court sentenced 37 opposition members and human rights defenders to prison terms of between four and 66 years. Amnesty International described the charges as "unfounded." Yet in November, a court of appeal upheld most verdicts.

In the past year, there have also been "positive examples where sustained collective mobilization led to the release of arbitrarily detained persons," Amnesty International's Safia Rayan said. Nevertheless, authorities had continued undermining human rights and the rule of law, Rayan added.

body.zh: 突尼斯政府正在加大对反对派人士、记者和民间社会的压力，引发了人们对镇压加深和民主制度逐步瓦解的新担忧。 突尼斯的人权问题日益引起人们的关注。周二，法院维持了对两名被指控犯有金融犯罪的突尼斯著名记者的判决。但媒体权利组织表示，这一裁决是一起“司法骚扰”案件，并认为所提出的指控缺乏证据。 听证会前，国际特赦组织敲响了警钟，指责突尼斯当局加大对非政府组织的压力，并利用法律手段解散此类团体。倡导人权、移民保护、选举监督和反腐败的非政府组织受到的影响最大。 国际特赦组织的萨菲亚·拉扬 (Safia Rayan) 告诉德国之声：“数十个非政府组织面临被解散的风险，而其他组织则受到起诉。” “对民间社会和独立媒体的打压正在加剧，并威胁到他们的生存。” Last week, the UN ' s High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, called on Tunisia to end its repression of opposition members and civil society groups.蒂尔克在日内瓦发表讲话时表示，人权活动人士正在被定罪。 温和派伊斯兰复兴运动党主席、84 岁的拉希德·加努奇 (Rached Ghannouchi) 的命运也引发了人们的担忧。据路透社报道，他是该国最著名的囚犯之一，目前已被判处约 50 年监禁。 2019 年当选的突尼斯总统凯斯·赛义德自 2021 年以来一直在巩固权力。他让突尼斯议会靠边站，削弱了司法机构，并对反对派成员和批评者采取行动。 专门研究民主结构的美国组织民主侵蚀联盟将赛义德的政府风格描述为“隐形威权主义”，民主制度逐渐受到破坏。该组织称，剩下的只是“民主的外表”。 一段时间以来，突尼斯当局一直在镇压持不同政见者。 2025 年 4 月，突尼斯法院判处 37 名反对派成员和人权捍卫者 4 至 66 年有期徒刑。国际特赦组织称这些指控“毫无根据”。然而，11 月，上诉法院维持了大部分判决。 国际特赦组织的萨菲亚·拉扬表示，去年也出现了“持续的集体动员导致被任意拘留者获释的积极例子”。然而，拉扬补充说，当局继续破坏人权和法治。 “镇压的程度......

reflection.en: The news from Tunisia highlights the vulnerability of a society when those in power act without restraint. Proverbs reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a dangerous predator, bringing fear and hardship upon the people. In such times, the call for justice and the protection of fundamental freedoms becomes ever more urgent.
reflection.zh: 突尼斯的新闻凸显了当掌权者肆无忌惮时，社会所面临的脆弱性。箴言提醒我们，邪恶的统治者可能像危险的捕食者，给人民带来恐惧和苦难。在这样的时刻，对正义和基本自由的呼吁变得更加紧迫。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.

title.en: Four audience members ejected from Eurovision over 'disruptive behaviour' during Israel set
title.zh: 四名观众因在以色列表演期间的“扰乱行为”被逐出欧洲歌唱大赛

summary.en: Four audience members were ejected from the Eurovision Song Contest semi-final due to disruptive behavior during Israel's performance. The Israeli contestant noted hearing boos from a small number of protesters as he took the stage.
summary.zh: 在欧洲歌唱大赛半决赛期间，四名观众因在以色列选手表演时行为不当而被驱逐出场。以色列选手表示，他在登台时听到了少数抗议者的嘘声。

body.en:
Four people have been thrown out of the first Eurovision Song Contest semi-final, which saw attempts to disrupt Israel's performance.

As 28-year-old Israeli singer Noam Bettan began his performance of Michelle during Tuesday's live show, a protester could be heard shouting "Stop, stop the genocide", and "Free, free Palestine".

Israel's participation in Eurovision 2026 has led to five countries pulling out of the world's biggest live televised music event.

In a joint statement, Austrian host broadcaster ORF and the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) said: "An audience of 10,000 fans in the Wiener Stadthalle at the first semi-final of the 70th Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna greeted every artist enthusiastically."

"ORF is broadcasting a clean audio feed live from audience microphones before and during every performer's song.

"One audience member, close to a microphone, loudly expressed their views as the Israeli artist began his performance, and during the song, which was heard on the live broadcast. They were later removed by security for continuing to disturb the audience.

"Three other people were also removed from the arena by security for disruptive behaviour."

Bettan told BBC television on Wednesday he was "aware" of what was happening in the audience.

"I heard there was booing and everything, and there was a moment of, like, a wow effect, you know? A little bit of shock," he said.

Five EBU broadcasters — from Iceland, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Spain — have boycotted this year's song contest over Israel's military action in Gaza.

Israel launched an offensive in Gaza after an assault led by Hamas — the political and military group that rules the Palestinian territory — in the south of the country on 7 October 2023 that killed 1,200 people, according to Israeli tallies.

More than 72,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since October 7, according to local health authorities.

Dean Vuletic, an academic and expert on Eurovision history, told SBS Croatian that while boycotts are not new to the competition, this year's anti-Israel protests demonstrate the need for better regulation of political influences on the event.

"The first boycott happened in 1969, when Austria boycotted Eurovision because the contest was being held in Spain while dictator Francisco Franco was ruling the country. Eurovision has a history when it comes to boycotts, but this is still the largest political boycott, and that is why the situation is concerning," he said.

body.zh: 首届欧洲歌唱大赛半决赛中有四人被淘汰，有人试图扰乱以色列的表现。 当 28 岁的以色列歌手诺姆·贝坦在周二的现场表演中开始表演米歇尔时，可以听到一名抗议者高喊“停止，停止种族灭绝”和“自由，自由巴勒斯坦”。 以色列参加 2026 年欧洲歌唱大赛已导致五个国家退出这一世界上最大的现场电视音乐盛会。 奥地利主办广播公司 ORF 和欧洲广播联盟 (EBU) 在一份联合声明中表示：“第 70 届欧洲歌唱大赛第一场半决赛在维也纳举行，维也纳体育场的 10,000 名观众热情地迎接了每一位艺术家。” “ORF 在每位表演者演唱歌曲之前和期间通过观众麦克风现场直播清晰的音频。 “当这位以色列艺术家开始表演时，一名靠近麦克风的观众在现场直播中听到的歌曲中大声表达了他们的观点。他们后来因继续扰乱观众而被保安带走。 “另外三人也因扰乱行为而被保安带离竞技场。” 贝坦周三告诉英国广播公司电视台，他“知道”观众中发生的事情。 “我听说现场响起了嘘声和一切，有一瞬间，就像是一种哇的效果，你知道吗？有点震惊，”他说。 来自冰岛、爱尔兰、荷兰、斯洛文尼亚和西班牙的五家 EBU 广播公司因以色列在加沙的军事行动而抵制今年的歌曲比赛。 据以色列统计，2023 年 10 月 7 日，统治巴勒斯坦领土的政治和军事组织哈马斯在该国南部发动袭击，造成 1,200 人死亡，随后以色列对加沙发动了攻势。 据当地卫生部门称，自 10 月 7 日以来，已有超过 72,500 名巴勒斯坦人在加沙被杀。 欧洲电视网历史学者兼专家迪恩·武莱蒂克 (Dean Vuletic) 告诉 SBS 克罗地亚语，虽然抵制对这项赛事来说并不新鲜，但今年的反以色列抗议活动表明，需要更好地监管对该赛事的政治影响。 “第一次抵制发生在1969年，当时奥地利抵制欧洲歌唱大赛，因为该比赛是在独裁者弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥统治该国的西班牙举行的。欧洲歌唱大赛有抵制的历史，但这仍然是最大规模的政治抵制，这就是情况令人担忧的原因，”他说。 SBS 是 EBU 的准成员和澳大利亚官方欧洲电视网广播公司，表示今年将继续参与和报道比赛，认为退出将损害其编辑独立性，并且……

reflection.en: The incident at Eurovision highlights how public expressions of strong emotion can disrupt shared spaces. Proverbs 15:1 reminds us that while harsh words or actions can escalate tension, a gentle response has the power to de-escalate conflict. This wisdom encourages us to consider the impact of our conduct, even in moments of passionate disagreement.
reflection.zh: 欧洲歌唱大赛上的事件表明，公众强烈的情绪表达会扰乱共享空间。箴言15:1提醒我们，严厉的言语或行为会加剧紧张，而温柔的回应却有能力化解冲突。这智慧鼓励我们在充满激情的异议时刻，也要思考自己行为的影响。

verse.textEn: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
verse.textZh: 回答柔和，使怒消退；言语暴戾，触动怒气。

title.en: Football chief seeks Iraqi citizenship for Australian coach Graham Arnold
title.zh: 足球总监寻求为澳大利亚教练格雷厄姆·阿诺德办理伊拉克公民身份

summary.en: Former Australian national coach Graham Arnold has become a hero in the Middle Eastern country, leading to the football chief seeking Iraqi citizenship for him.
summary.zh: 前澳大利亚国家队教练格雷厄姆·阿诺德在中东国家成为英雄，该国足球总监正寻求为其办理伊拉克公民身份。

body.en:
Iraq's governing football body has told former Australian football coach Graham Arnold it has sought citizenship on his behalf, after he led their national team to their first FIFA World Cup in 40 years.

Arnold, who coached Australia at the 2022 FIFA World Cup, was appointed as Iraq's head coach in May last year and tasked specifically with helping the team qualify.

They did so by defeating Bolivia 2-1 in April, making the upcoming tournament in the United States the country's first since 1986.

In a video posted on social media, Iraqi Football Association president Adnan Dirjal thanked Arnold for his contribution to the country and wished him "continued success and prosperity" in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which is just under a month away.

"A full year has passed, and today we enter the second year, and we are very proud of you," Dirjal says.

"Truly, and thank God, you achieved the dream for millions of Iraqis, for more than 46 million Iraqis — you and all the heroic young men who delivered an honourable performance despite all the challenges and circumstances over forty years."

The official then tells Arnold about the citizenship request, as the Australian appears surprised.

"And as we promised you after qualifying for the World Cup, we will make a request through the respected prime minister, who was and still is the biggest supporter in achieving this accomplishment and all our work in the federation during the past four years.

"I told you that we would request Iraqi citizenship for you, and we have sent a request to the prime minister regarding that."

In a separate video, Arnold speaks to the country's prime minister Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani, accompanied by Dirjal and a translator.

"And the Iraqi mentality was the main point, that we would win. The fighting mentality of the players. And that's what we need to take to the World Cup," he continues.

In a third video, Arnold is shown shaking hands with al-Sudani and tells him: "Now we will shock the world."

Arnold was met with wild scenes as he arrived back in Australia after securing Iraq's World Cup spot, as hundreds of Iraqi Australians cheered him and celebrated the win.

A former Socceroo, Arnold later turned to coaching, and took the head Socceroos role in 2018 after that year's FIFA World Cup in Russia.

Iraq's World Cup campaign was complicated by the war in the Middle East, with travel for the team becoming a logistical nightmare.

Attention now turns to the World Cup being hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico, where Iraq will face France, Senegal and Norway in the group stage from 12 June.

body.zh: 伊拉克足球管理机构告诉前澳大利亚足球教练格雷厄姆·阿诺德，在他带领国家队40年来首次参加国际足联世界杯后，他们已代表他寻求公民身份。 阿诺德曾在2022年世界杯上执教澳大利亚队，去年5月被任命为伊拉克队主教练，专门负责帮助球队晋级。 今年 4 月，他们以 2-1 击败玻利维亚，使即将在美国举行的世界杯成为自 1986 年以来首次在美国举行。 在社交媒体上发布的一段视频中，伊拉克足协主席阿德南·迪贾尔感谢阿诺德对国家的贡献，并祝愿他在距离2026年国际足联世界杯还有不到一个月的时间里“继续取得成功和繁荣”。 “整整一年过去了，今天我们进入了第二年，我们为你们感到非常自豪，”迪加尔说。 “确实，感谢上帝，你们实现了数百万伊拉克人、超过4600万伊拉克人的梦想——你们和所有英勇的年轻人，尽管四十年来面临各种挑战和环境，但仍取得了光荣的业绩。” 然后，这位官员告诉阿诺德有关公民身份的申请，这位澳大利亚人似乎很惊讶。 “正如我们在获得世界杯资格后向你们承诺的那样，我们将通过尊敬的总理提出请求，他过去是、现在仍然是实现这一成就以及过去四年我们在足协所有工作的最大支持者。 “我告诉过你，我们会为你申请伊拉克公民身份，我们已就此向总理发出请求。” 在另一段视频中，阿诺德在迪贾尔和一名翻译的陪同下与该国总理穆罕默德·什叶派·苏达尼进行了交谈。 “伊拉克人的心态是重点，我们会赢。球员的战斗心态。这就是我们参加世界杯所需要的，”他继续说道。 在第三段视频中，阿诺德与苏达尼握手并告诉他：“现在我们将震惊世界。” 阿诺德在获得伊拉克世界杯参赛资格后返回澳大利亚时，遇到了疯狂的场面，数百名伊拉克澳大利亚人为他欢呼并庆祝胜利。 阿诺德曾是一名澳大利亚足球运动员，后来转而担任教练，并于 2018 年俄罗斯世界杯结束后担任澳大利亚足球队主教练。 伊拉克世界杯的征程因中东战争而变得复杂，球队的旅行成为后勤上的噩梦。 现在的注意力转向由美国、加拿大和墨西哥主办的世界杯，伊拉克将从 6 月 12 日起在小组赛中对阵法国、塞内加尔和挪威。 您可以在 SBS、SBS VICELAND 和 SBS On Demand 上免费独家直播观看 2026 年 FIFA 世界杯™ 的所有 104 场比赛。 有关 SBS 新闻的最新消息，...

reflection.en: This story beautifully illustrates the spirit of welcoming the stranger, as a foreign coach is embraced and honored for his contributions. It reminds us of the biblical call to love foreigners, recognizing our shared humanity and the potential for connection across national boundaries.
reflection.zh: 这个故事生动地展现了欢迎异乡人的精神，一位外国教练因其贡献而受到接纳和尊敬。它提醒我们圣经中爱护寄居者的呼召，认识到我们共同的人性以及跨越国界建立联系的潜力。

verse.textEn: And you are to love those who are foreigners, for you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要怜爱寄居的，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: An empty $1.37 billion facility and 'upskilling' staff: Inside Australia's hantavirus test
title.zh: 一个耗资13.7亿美元的空置设施和“技能提升”的工作人员：澳大利亚汉坦病毒检测的内幕

summary.en: Australia's response to a hantavirus outbreak, which originated on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean, involved an empty $1.37 billion facility and staff requiring 'upskilling,' contrasting with the approaches taken by other nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚对源自大西洋一艘游轮的汉坦病毒疫情的应对措施，包括一个耗资13.7亿美元的空置设施和需要‘技能提升’的工作人员，这与其他国家的做法形成对比。

body.en:
Preparations are underway at a quarantine facility in Western Australia set to receive four Australians who will soon be repatriated from a hantavirus-hit cruise ship.

The centre has largely sat idle since it was unveiled at the tail-end of the COVID-19 pandemic, but now faces its first real test, as six people potentially exposed to the deadly hantavirus are set to stay for at least three weeks.

Dutch cruise-liner MV Hondius ' trip to some of the most remote islands in the world was interrupted last month, after an outbreak of the rodent-borne hantavirus killed three people, infected eight others and created chaos for governments around the world now tasked with safely repatriating their passengers.

While authorities work to understand how the outbreak started , the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has scrambled to find a plane capable of the long journey between the Netherlands and Perth — and a crew willing to quarantine for 42 days after the trip.

On Wednesday, the federal government confirmed a plane had been secured and that the necessary clearances and approvals were being made for the trip.

Once they touch down in Perth, the four Australians plus one permanent resident, a New Zealander, and the flight's crew will spend their quarantine period at the Bullsbrook Centre ﻿for National Resilience, 40km north-east of Perth.

The purpose-built 500-bed quarantine facility was completed in 2022, at the tail end of the COVID-19 pandemic.

It is one of three of its kind in the country, equipped with specialised ventilation systems, and designed to ensure food and staff can move safely around the facility without risk of cross-contamination.

Every surface in the centre can be easily disinfected, and there are specialist medical facilities on site.

For the remainder of their quarantine period, the passengers of the MV Hondius will receive 24-hour care and be closely monitored for symptoms of the disease, which has a 30 to 50 per cent mortality rate.

The Australian response stands in contrast to other countries' approaches to the outbreak, where many asymptomatic passengers who were on board the ship are self-isolating at home.

Some 22 affected travellers from the United Kingdom will spend 72 hours in hospital before being sent home to self-isolate for a further 42 days.

Eighteen passengers have returned to the United States, including one travel blogger who has been documenting his time in quarantine.

Some of them are being screened at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in the city of Omaha, and two are in Atlanta, Georgia.

They will each receive individual care plans, which will require them to either self-isolate or remain at a facility.

body.zh: 西澳大利亚州的一个检疫设施正在进行准备工作，准备接收四名澳大利亚人，他们很快将从一艘受汉坦病毒袭击的游轮上被遣返回国。 该中心自新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行末期推出以来，基本上一直处于闲置状态，但现在面临着第一次真正的考验，因为六名可能接触致命汉坦病毒的人将在该中心停留至少三周。 上个月，荷兰邮轮 MV Hondius 前往世界上一些最偏远岛屿的旅程被中断，原因是啮齿类动物传播的汉坦病毒爆发，造成三人死亡、八人感染，并给目前负责安全遣返乘客的世界各国政府造成混乱。 在当局努力了解疫情是如何爆发的同时，外交贸易部也在忙着寻找一架能够在荷兰和珀斯之间进行长途旅行的飞机，以及愿意在旅行后隔离 42 天的机组人员。 周三，联邦政府确认一架飞机已经安全，并且正在为这次旅行进行必要的许可和批准。 一旦飞机降落在珀斯，这四名澳大利亚人加上一名永久居民、一名新西兰人以及机组人员将在位于珀斯东北 40 公里的布尔斯布鲁克国家抗灾中心度过隔离期。 这个专门建造的拥有 500 个床位的检疫设施于 2022 年竣工，当时正值新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行的尾声。 它是该国三个此类设施之一，配备了专门的通风系统，旨在确保食品和工作人员可以在设施内安全移动，而没有交叉污染的风险。 中心的每个表面都可以轻松消毒，并且现场设有专业的医疗设施。 在剩余的隔离期内，MV Hondius 号的乘客将接受 24 小时护理，并密切监测该疾病的症状，该疾病的死亡率为 30% 至 50%。 澳大利亚的应对措施与其他国家应对疫情的方法形成鲜明对比，船上许多无症状的乘客正在家中自我隔离。 大约 22 名来自英国的受影响旅客将在医院住院 72 小时，然后被送回家继续自我隔离 42 天。 十八名乘客已返回美国，其中包括一名记录自己隔离时间的旅游博主。 其中一些正在奥马哈市的内布拉斯加大学医学中心进行筛查，另外两个在佐治亚州亚特兰大。 他们每个人都将收到个人护理计划，这将要求他们自我隔离或留在设施中。 在荷兰、加拿大、瑞士和德国，乘客将...

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has started his trip to Beijing by telling Chinese President Xi Jinping "it's an honour to be your friend", even as his counterpart offered a cautionary warning about avoiding a possible clash between the two nations.

The stark contrast in tone underscored just how far apart the leaders remain on thorny issues, including the war in Iran , trade disputes and the US relationship with Taiwan — and suggests that Trump and Xi's highly anticipated meetings are likely to be stronger on pageantry and symbolism than major breakthroughs.

In remarks before their meeting at the Great Hall of the People moved behind closed doors, Trump was full of platitudes, saying of Xi: "You're a great leader. Sometimes people don't like me saying it, but I say it anyway, because it's true."

"It's an honour to be with you. It's an honour to be your friend," Trump said before promising that "the relationship between China and the USA is going to be better than ever before".

Xi was less positive, expressing hope that the US and China could avoid conflict while saying that history and the world were asking "whether the two countries can transcend the 'Thucydides Trap' and forge a new model for relations between major powers".

China's leader used a term popular in foreign policy studies, referring to the idea that when a rising power threatens to displace an established power, the result is often war.

"Cooperation benefits both sides, while confrontation harms both," Xi said. "The two countries should be partners rather than rivals, achieve success together and pursue common prosperity, and chart a correct path for major-country relations in the new era."

The remarks from each followed a sweeping greeting for Trump outside the Great Hall of the People, an imposing building on Tiananmen Square that houses China's legislature. Cannons boomed a welcome salute, and a band played the US and Chinese national anthems.

The hall featured giant, red-carpeted steps and huge expanses of marble, where soldiers hung large American and Chinese flags. School children in bright colours offered a welcome routine, jumping as the girls waved flowers and the boys hoisted US and Chinese flags while the two leaders walked past them.

The Republican US president is set to visit the Temple of Heaven, a religious complex dating to the 15th century that symbolises the relationship between heaven and earth. Trump and Xi will also attend a state banquet.

Donald Trump and Xi Jinping have been holding talks in the Chinese capital, Beijing, with a raft of meetings and events taking place on Thursday and Friday.

The US leader was greeted with a gun salute, cheering children and a tour of the stunning 15th Century Temple of Heaven.

Trump is also joined in Beijing by tech bosses, including Tesla's Elon Musk and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and Trump's son Eric.

On Thursday evening, a lavish banuquet at the Great Hall of the People was held in honour of the occasion.

BBC reporters were able to see the banquet menu, with the main course including lobster in tomato soup, Beijing roast duck and pan-fried pork bun.

In a banquet speech, President Xi called it a "historic visit", adding "the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation" and "Make America great again" can go hand in hand.

China-US relations are the most important bilateral relations in the world, Xi says.

Their relations concern the well-being of the two countries of 1.7 billion population, and the interests of over 8 billion people in the world, he added.

He then invited Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to visit the White House on 24 September.

Among those spotted at Thurday's banquet were Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Apple CEO Tim Cook, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Eric and Lara Trump.

Trump landed in Beijing on Wednesday evening, where he was greeted by youths waving American and Chinese flags as he walked the red carpet with Vice President of China Han Zheng.

On Thursday, Trump was welcomed at an arrival ceremony with Xi at China's Great Hall of the People.

After shaking hands, Trump and Xi walked the red carpet and inspected Chinese troops who lined up in impeccably neat rows.

Dozens of children also lined up along the red carpet and waved mini flags and bouquets.

Joining Trump on his trip to China are some of the US's top business leaders, including Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, and Larry Fink of BlackRock.

title.en: Flattery and fanfare as Trump welcomed to China - but thorny issues remain

summary.en: The leaders of the world's two superpowers were all smiles for the cameras during the US president's visit to Beijing, despite significant unresolved issues between their nations.
summary.zh: 美国总统访问北京期间，世界两大超级大国的领导人在镜头前笑容满面，尽管两国之间仍存在重大的未决问题。

body.en:
Xi Jinping threw a grand welcome for Donald Trump on the first day of a visit that could reset ties between the rival superpowers.

The military honour guard lined up outside the Great Hall of the People to welcome Trump, complete with a gun salute and a band playing the US national anthem. The president paused twice to say hello to schoolchildren cheering with Chinese and American flags.

As he shook hands with Xi, he leaned in to pat him on the arm in what appeared to be a gesture of warmth. And he lavished praise on his host.

"You're a great leader. I say it to everybody," he declared in what appeared to be unscripted remarks. Later, on his tour of the 15th Century Temple of Heaven, he remarked to reporters that China was beautiful. At the banquet this evening, he called the talks a "cherished" opportunity.

It was a remarkable day given Trump built up his political brand by talking tough on China.

"We can't continue to allow China to rape our country, and that's what they're doing," he told a campaign rally in 2016.

In 2020, he claimed China has "ripped off the United States like no one has ever done before", and described the Covid-19 pandemic as the "Chinese virus". Before returning to power, he vowed to "make China pay".

At the height of the trade war last year, the two sides had levied tariffs that crossed 100% on each other. A fragile truce followed but one of the main questions hanging over this visit is whether that will last, and what deal would take its place?

The others are around Iran - can Beijing help broker a deal? – and Taiwan, the US ally and self-governed island that China claims as its territory.

Beijing put on a spectacle designed to flatter Trump ahead of any deal to prove China's door is open to guests. However, soon after talks began, state media published comments from Xi making clear that tensions over Taiwan could prove challenging.

But the meticulous choreography was not just for the benefit of Trump and the 30 CEOs who accompanied him. It was also a show of strength, which Beijing knows will be beamed live across the US and the world.

"We are witnessing a historical change," says John Delury, a senior fellow from the Centre on US-China Relations at the Asia Society.

"I hesitate to put too much on this specific summit, but the inexorable rise of China to a place where it is legitimately rivalling the U.S. - that is now happening before our eyes. Beijing is now the second world capital."

President Xi has been eager to portray himself as a stable global leader in contrast to a mercurial US president. Given the size of China's economy, a number of world leaders, including those from US allies such as Canada, the UK and Germany, have turned up, eager to do a deal with Beijing.

title.en: What to know as Trump visits Xi in China
title.zh: 特朗普访问中国，你需要知道什么

summary.en: Trump has landed in Beijing for the first visit by a US leader since his own in 2017.
summary.zh: 特朗普已抵达北京，这是自他2017年访问以来，美国领导人首次到访中国。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is in Beijing on the first trip to China by an American leader since in his own previous visit, during his first term in 2017.

He was given a spectacular welcome at the Great Hall of the People. The two leaders shook hands on the red carpet before entering a room for their bilateral meeting.

The talks lasted around two hours, longer than expected. Trump called the talks "great", but there are few details on whether any progress was made on key issues.

The trip was originally meant to be held in March but rescheduled after the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran.

The main focus of the talks is expected to be the current tense trade relationship between the two superpowers.

Trump said he would ask Xi to "open up" China's economy to major tech companies.

He added that he also expected a "long talk" about Iran, though he insisted he did not need China's help to end the conflict.

He said Xi had been "relatively good" on Iran, adding that it would be an "exciting trip" and "a lot of good things are going to happen".

Xi meanwhile is expected to press for an end to US arms sales to Taiwan, and an extension of the trade truce agreed in October that halted tariff escalation between the US and China.

Commentary in Chinese media also suggested Beijing was looking for a "better future" with the US, and a relationship that would "add more stability and certainty" to a turbulent world.

At the bilateral meeting, Xi told Trump that Taiwan was the most important issue in their relationship and warned that if it was not handled properly, there would be "clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy", according to state media.

He also raised the issue of "Taiwan independence", warning that the US must "exercise extra caution" when it comes to the self-governed island.

China claims self-governed Taiwan as part of its territory - but the island sees itself as distinct.

The US has formal ties with Beijing rather than Taiwan, and has walked a tight diplomatic rope for decades. But it remains a powerful ally of Taiwan and is the island's biggest arms supplier.

But last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Taiwan would be a topic of conversation at the summit, with a view to preventing the issue becoming a source of tension between the US and China.

In his opening remarks to Trump at the bilateral meeting, Xi mentioned the Thucydides Trap.

It's a political term popularised by American scholar Graham Allison that has been used to describe the US-China relationship.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达北京，这是他自2017年第一个任期内访问中国以来美国领导人首次访华。 他将与中国国家主席习近平举行为期两天的会谈，原定于三月份举行，但在美国和以色列对伊朗发动袭击后重新安排。 预计会谈的主要焦点将是两个超级大国之间当前紧张的贸易关系。 特朗普表示，他将要求习近平向大型科技公司“开放”中国经济。 他补充说，他还预计就伊朗问题进行“长谈”，但他坚称不需要中国的帮助来结束冲突。 他表示，习近平对伊朗的态度“相对较好”，并补充说，这将是一次“令人兴奋的旅行”，“很多好事将会发生”。 与此同时，预计习近平将敦促美国停止向台湾出售武器，并延长十月份达成的贸易休战协议，以阻止中美之间的关税升级。 中国媒体的评论还暗示，北京正在寻求与美国的“更好的未来”，以及一种能为动荡的世界“增添更多稳定性和确定性”的关系。 特朗普于当地时间周三晚上乘坐空军一号抵达北京，周四开始主要访问。 在两国领导人举行双边会谈之前，美国总统预计将出席在人民大会堂举行的习近平抵达仪式。 周五，特朗普将访问中南海，这是中国领导人生活和工作的一处高档大院。这次访问将以与习近平的“友谊照片”和握手为特色。 在与习近平再次举行双边会晤并享用工作午餐后，特朗普将返回机场参加离境仪式，然后返回美国。 陪同特朗普出访的还有美国主要企业和科技公司的首席执行官。 随总统正式访问北京的人员包括英伟达公司的黄仁勋、苹果公司的蒂姆·库克、特斯拉和 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克、贝莱德的拉里·芬克，以及来自 Meta、Visa、摩根大通、波音、嘉吉等公司的其他高管。 黄仁勋的加入值得注意，因为英伟达的先进人工智能（AI）芯片是中美竞争的主要焦点。 他并未出现在最初的名单中，但受到特朗普的亲自邀请，并被发现在阿拉斯加中途停留期间登上了空军一号。 自 2025 年以来，这个问题有所缓解，其中大部分时间中国和美国似乎处于贸易战的边缘。 但由于永久解决方案仍难以达成，双方仍有很多话题可谈。 预计特朗普将推动中国增加从美国重要行业购买商品，包括大豆和飞机零部件。 北京来了...

Leaders who actively seek understanding and common ground embody the spirit of peacemaking, striving to build bridges rather than walls between nations. Such efforts, though complex, are vital for a world yearning for harmony.

title.en: China goes electric, but can it get off coal?
title.zh: 中国走向电气化，但能否摆脱煤炭？

summary.en: The world's clean energy superpower also emits the most CO2. But coal-fired power may have peaked as China electrifies its economy with ever more renewables.
summary.zh: 作为全球清洁能源超级大国，中国也是二氧化碳排放量最大的国家。然而，随着中国经济日益电气化并更多地采用可再生能源，燃煤发电可能已达到峰值。

body.en:
The world's clean energy superpower also emits the most CO2. But coal-fired power may have peaked as China electrifies its economy with ever more renewables.

China is undergoing a renewable energy revolution. In 2025 alone, it added nearly 450 gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity, which was more solar and twice as much wind as the rest of the world combined.

Before 2010, China had only limited renewable energy . Today, electricity generated by huge wind and solar farms that stretch out across mountains, deserts, on rooftops and off the coast, account for a quarter of electricity production.

The country achieved the goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030 five years ahead of schedule. China also produces over 80% of the world's photovoltaic panels, helping drive down costs and accelerating the clean energy transition globally.

Its quest to rid itself of dependence on foreign oil and gas has been the chief inspiration for the rapid expansion of domestic energy sources and electrification, says Tim Buckley, director of Australian think tank Climate Energy Finance.

Beijing invested early in electric vehicles , and batteries, noted Buckley. Fossil fuel-free vehicles now account for more than half of all car sales in China, compared with about 19% in the European Union.

But the clean energy boom has not displaced coal, the most polluting fossil fuel. The country remains the world's largest emitter of carbon dioxide and continues to exploit its own vast coal reserves in pursuit of energy self-reliance. China consumes over 50% of global supply, in part because it's the only fossil fuel it doesn't have to import. 

In January and February 2026 alone, China added 20 gigawatts of coal-fired power capacity — nearly half the amount of new renewables added over the same period. This partly explains why the country is not on track to meet its 2060 carbon neutrality goal, according to climate think tank, Carbon Tracker. 

The contradiction is at the center of scrutiny over China's latest five year-plan (5YP), a policy blueprint that will shape the economy through 2031 and determine whether the country can meet its climate pledges and help curb planetary heating.  

In 2015, China signed onto the Paris climate agreement, which aims to limit global temperature rise to well below 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 Fahrenheit) or preferably 1.5C, compared to pre-industrial levels. The country then committed to peak CO2 emissions before 2030, and to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.

title.en: China warns Trump over Taiwan question at high-stakes summit
title.zh: 中国在高风险峰会上就台湾问题警告特朗普

summary.en: Chinese state media reported that Xi Jinping raised the question of Taiwan during his meeting with Donald Trump. The pair held talks for about two hours. Follow live.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Chinese state media reported that Xi Jinping raised the question of Taiwan during his meeting with Donald Trump. The pair held talks for about two hours. Follow live.

China's President Xi Jinping has promised to help the US open the Strait of Hormuz , which Iran has kept largely shuttered since the US and Israel first attacked it on February 28, according to US President Donald Trump.

Speaking to Fox News' "Hannity" show from Beijing on Thursday, shortly after a meeting with Xi, Trump said of his Chinese counterpart: "He'd like to see the Hormuz Strait open, and said 'if I can be of any help whatsoever, I would like to help.'"

Trump also said that Xi vowed not to arm Iran in its conflict against the US and Israel.

"He said he's not going to give military equipment... he said that strongly," Trump said.

US officials traveling with President Donald Trump to China have sought to downplay what appeared to be casting aside the question of Taiwan in talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who directly warned Washington over the self-governed island.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told US business news network CNBC that Trump would say more on Taiwan "in the coming days."

"It wouldn't be a US-China summit without the Taiwan issue coming up," Bessent said. "President Trump understands the issues here and understands the sensitivities around all this. Anyone who has been saying otherwise does not understand the negotiating style of Donald Trump."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio meanwhile stressed Washington's policy toward Taiwan remained "unchanged."

"US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today. It was raised. They always raise it on their side. We always make clear our position, and we move on to the other topics," Rubio told NBC news.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC he believes China will act to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz , calling it firmly in China’s own interest.

It comes after President Donald Trump discussed the war with Iran with China's President Xi Jinping during their meeting in Beijing.

In response to the US-Israeli strikes , Iran has effectively closed the strategic Strait of Hormuz to Gulf oil and gas exports, sending prices soaring and forcing countries around the world to scramble for alternative supplies.

The White House says both leaders agreed the Strait of Hormuz must be open, and that Iran should never acquire nuclear weapons.

China is Iran’s closest major partner and its biggest oil customer, giving Beijing significant leverage.

title.en: Trump heralds friendship with China as Xi warns of possible confrontation at summit

summary.en: US President Trump has begun a visit to China, the first by a US president in nearly a decade. Discussions are expected to cover tariffs, Taiwan, and Iran, with the ongoing war in the Middle East also a significant topic.
summary.zh: 美国总统特朗普已开始对中国进行访问，这是近十年来美国总统首次访华。预计会谈将涵盖关税、台湾和伊朗等议题，中东地区的持续战争也将是一个重要议题。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has started his trip to Beijing by telling Chinese President Xi Jinping "it's an honour to be your friend", even as his counterpart offered a cautionary warning about avoiding a possible clash between the two nations.

The stark contrast in tone underscored just how far apart the leaders remain on thorny issues, including the war in Iran , trade disputes and the US relationship with Taiwan — and suggests that Trump and Xi's highly anticipated meetings are likely to be stronger on pageantry and symbolism than major breakthroughs.

In remarks before their meeting at the Great Hall of the People moved behind closed doors, Trump was full of platitudes, saying of Xi: "You're a great leader. Sometimes people don't like me saying it, but I say it anyway, because it's true."

"It's an honour to be with you. It's an honour to be your friend," Trump said before promising that "the relationship between China and the USA is going to be better than ever before".

Xi was less positive, expressing hope that the US and China could avoid conflict while saying that history and the world were asking "whether the two countries can transcend the 'Thucydides Trap' and forge a new model for relations between major powers".

China's leader used a term popular in foreign policy studies, referring to the idea that when a rising power threatens to displace an established power, the result is often war.

"Cooperation benefits both sides, while confrontation harms both," Xi said. "The two countries should be partners rather than rivals, achieve success together and pursue common prosperity, and chart a correct path for major-country relations in the new era."

The remarks from each followed a sweeping greeting for Trump outside the Great Hall of the People, an imposing building on Tiananmen Square that houses China's legislature. Cannons boomed a welcome salute, and a band played the US and Chinese national anthems.

The hall featured giant, red-carpeted steps and huge expanses of marble, where soldiers hung large American and Chinese flags. School children in bright colours offered a welcome routine, jumping as the girls waved flowers and the boys hoisted US and Chinese flags while the two leaders walked past them.

The Republican US president is set to visit the Temple of Heaven, a religious complex dating to the 15th century that symbolises the relationship between heaven and earth. Trump and Xi will also attend a state banquet.

title.en: As his China trip begins, Trump insists he doesn't need Xi's help on Iran
title.zh: 特朗普访华之初坚称伊朗问题无需习近平帮助

summary.en: Donald Trump is set to meet Chinese president Xi Jinping for high-stakes talks on Friday and Saturday.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普定于周五和周六与中国国家主席习近平举行高风险会谈。

body.en:
Donald Trump was due to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday, the first visit to China by a US president in nearly a decade, as he seeks to ramp up trade despite potential friction over Taiwan and Iran.

Leaving Washington DC on Wednesday on a trip that was delayed by his war, Trump said he expected a "long talk" with counterpart Xi Jinping about Iran, which relies on China as the top customer for its US-sanctioned oil.

But he also played down disagreements on Iran, saying that Xi has been "relatively good, to be honest with you".

"I don't think we need any help with Iran. We'll win it one way or the other. We'll win it peacefully or otherwise," Trump told reporters as he left the White House.

This week's trip — the first since Trump visited in 2017 — will involve high-stakes talks with Xi on Friday and Saturday, during a packed itinerary that includes a state banquet and tea reception.

Trump said on Tuesday that he would speak to Xi about US arms sales to Taiwan, the self-governing island claimed by China — a departure from historic US insistence that it will not consult China on its support to the island.

China's controls on rare earth exports and the countries' raucous trade relationship are among the topics expected to be taken up by the heads of the world's top two economies.

The tense buildup to the superpower summit was already visible on Wednesday on the streets of Beijing, with police monitoring major intersections and checking the ID cards of passengers on the metro, Agence France-Presse (AFP) journalists saw.

"It's definitely a big deal," said Wen Wen, a 24-year-old woman travelling from the eastern city of Nanjing, when asked by AFP about Trump's visit.

"Some progress will certainly be made," she said, noting that she hopes China and the United States can ensure "lasting peace" despite "recent instability in the global situation".

Trade ties between China and the US have been fraught in recent years. The two sides are currently maintaining a one-year truce in their tariff war reached at Trump and Xi's last meeting in South Korea in October.

China's major surplus in trade with the United States has long irritated Trump, who slapped tariffs on the country's goods during his first term in office.

Trump will be accompanied in China by a large group of top US business executives, including Tesla's Elon Musk and Apple's Tim Cook, the White House has said.

The highly anticipated summit comes at an uncertain time for China's economy, which has struggled in recent years with sluggish domestic spending and a protracted debt crisis in the once-booming property sector.

body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普定于周三抵达北京，这是美国总统近十年来首次访问中国，尽管台湾和伊朗问题可能存在摩擦，但他仍寻求扩大贸易。 特朗普周三离开华盛顿特区，开始他因战争而推迟的行程，他表示，他预计与习近平就伊朗问题进行“长谈”，伊朗依赖中国作为美国制裁石油的最大客户。 但他也淡化了在伊朗问题上的分歧，称习近平“老实说，相对不错”。 “我认为我们在伊朗问题上不需要任何帮助。我们会以一种或另一种方式赢得它。我们会以和平或其他方式赢得它，”特朗普在离开白宫时告诉记者。 本周的访问是特朗普自 2017 年访问以来的首次访问，周五和周六将与习近平进行高风险会谈，行程紧凑，包括国宴和茶会。 特朗普周二表示，他将与习近平讨论美国向中国声称拥有主权的台湾岛出售武器的问题，这与美国历来坚称不会就对台湾岛的支持问题征求中国意见的立场背道而驰。 中国对稀土出口的控制以及两国紧张的贸易关系预计将成为世界两大经济体领导人讨论的话题。 法新社记者看到，周三，北京街头已经出现了超级大国峰会的紧张气氛，警察监视着主要十字路口，并检查地铁乘客的身份证。 “这绝对是一件大事，”来自东部城市南京的 24 岁女性文文在被法新社问及特朗普的访问时说。 “肯定会取得一些进展，”她说，并指出，尽管“全球局势最近不稳定”，但她希望中国和美国能够确保“持久和平”。 近年来，中美之间的贸易关系充满挑战。两国目前正在维持特朗普和习近平十月份在韩国举行最后一次会晤时达成的为期一年的关税战停战协议。 中国对美国的巨额贸易顺差长期以来一直激怒特朗普，他在第一个任期内对中国商品征收关税。 白宫表示，特朗普将由一大批美国企业高管陪同访问中国，其中包括特斯拉的埃隆·马斯克和苹果的蒂姆·库克。 此次备受期待的峰会召开之际，中国经济正处于一个不确定的时期。近年来，中国经济因国内支出低迷和一度繁荣的房地产行业长期债务危机而陷入困境。 对于经营北京一家卡拉 OK 店的 30 岁李家豪来说，此次峰会不一定能解决中美关系中的所有问题——尽管他希望……
